clue.text: Still dream lives are changed for a second

indicators.note: the words before are changed into a new order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's quiet hopes are altered for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are changed' rearranges all fifteen letters of STILL DREAM LIVES; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-up in an Olympic final takes home the silver, so that person is the one who came second.

clue.text: Control an animal

definitions.meaning: a young bullock raised for beef

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a creature in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct a vehicle or person is to control it; a young castrated ox is also given this name.

clue.text: There is something attractive in a number of poems being set to music

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
odes are lyric poems
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Something appealing hides in a set of verses put to a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in', 'of' and 'being set to' are link words joining the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetic rock draws iron to it, and figuratively anything that draws people in.

clue.text: Trees a novice planted in town

indicators.note: something planted in the ground is set inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ems is a German spa town, Bad Ems
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Some trees that a beginner has put in around a town.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the learner's letter, goes inside EMS, the German spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tall broadleaved hardwoods, a common kind of shade tree.

clue.text: Strange horse without a carriage

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so the horse's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: An odd horse that has no carriage to pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the horse surrounds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome and eerie strikes us as weird and unsettling, as in a grim tale.

clue.text: Broken out and used although obedient

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are broken up and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Something worn out and spent, yet still compliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges OUT and USED; 'and' joins them and 'although' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dutiful person does as told, showing proper respect and compliance.

clue.text: One tailless animal in a row provides' something to drive

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for a row

parts.note: a line is a row of things
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the animal loses its final letter, its tail

parts.note: a mouse is a small animal

explanation.surface: A creature lacking its tail sits in a queue and offers transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts MOUSE to MOUS; with I that goes 'in' LINE. The apostrophe in 'provides'' is a print slip; the word is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large luxurious car is a vehicle someone sits behind the wheel of, often with a chauffeur.

clue.text: People who appear in nice nighties

indicators.note: the letters wanted show up within the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: Folk who are seen wearing pretty nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'niCE NIghties'. They were the tribe of Boudicca in ancient Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a tribe of eastern Britain in Roman times, so a people.

clue.text: A company of the line provided by a group of irregular soldiers?

indicators.note: the company belongs to the line, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a train runs on the railway line
a band is a company of people

explanation.surface: A railway company turns out to be a set of part-time troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' is a link. The question mark admits the fun: a BAND on the railway line. Historically this was a London citizen militia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tudor and Stuart England, citizen militias were drilled companies of part-time, non-regular fighters.

clue.text: Finish with record-maker caught and confined to a certain area

parts.note: an end is a finish
EMI is a British record company
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Ending up with the label that made the disc, nabbed and penned in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'and' are links. EMI is a long-established British record label.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or species native to or restricted to one region is described this way.

clue.text: Vale artist has something to paint in

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe is a famous valley in Greece
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter from the valley owns some paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link. TEMPE is the classical Greek valley; RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-based pigment is a painting medium, the one used in many medieval panels.

clue.text: Got up as a flower

explanation.surface: Someone stood up dressed as a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of 'rise', meaning stood or climbed up; also a thorny garden bloom.

clue.text: Release from punishment when there are wild lions about

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running loose and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Being let off when big cats roam free nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges LIONS and ABOUT together; 'when there are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage, a priest's formal forgiveness frees the penitent from sin and its penalty.

clue.text: He is invested with land, when Edward starts away in charge

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: the start of the name is its opening letter

parts.note: off means away, as in 'be off'

explanation.surface: A landholder with Edward setting off while in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes E from Edward; E and OFF go 'in' FEE. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal law, a person granted a fief or estate holds that property in trust.

clue.text: Give the sack and the factory makes trouble

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
works is another word for a factory

explanation.surface: Laying people off, plus the plant, stirs up strife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'makes' are links. The sense is a burst of anger, as in 'there'll be fireworks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an angry outburst or row is called this, like sparks flying.

clue.text: Fish in the country to make oneself independent

indicators.note: the fish is put inside the name of the country

parts.note: France is a country
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Going fishing in rural France to get away from it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside; it is a nation. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To work for oneself, taking jobs from various clients rather than an employer.

clue.text: Plant which enables one to read superficially before the intention is re- versed

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly over the surface

indicators.note: the word for the intention is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: A shrub that lets someone skim-read before their aim is turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'is re- versed' is one word split across a line in print. 'which enables one to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub grown in gardens for red berries, so a plant.

clue.text: Woody place could give a chap a healthy colour if hatless

parts.note: man means a chap
points to the hat the chap is without, which goes between
a tan is a healthy-looking colour

explanation.surface: Going bareheaded could give a fellow a ruddy glow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a little story: a MAN without his HAT gets a TAN. 'could give' and 'if' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York island is Woody Allen's city, setting of his film of that name.

clue.text: Jackets for smokers?

definitions.meaning: short double-breasted coats worn by sailors
joints of cannabis, things for people who smoke

explanation.surface: Coats made for people who light up.
explanation.definitionFit: Short double-breasted sailors' coats; also slang for cannabis cigarettes, which are things smoked.

clue.text: A note from paper to politician, it gives one a + healthy look

definitions.text: it gives one a + healthy look

parts.note: the Sun is a British newspaper
la is a note of the sol-fa scale
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A memo passed from a newspaper to an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'to' set the note between paper and politician. The '+' in the definition is a print mark, not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultraviolet lamp gives the skin a tan, a bronzed glow.

clue.text: What a bird did with a broken reed pen

indicators.note: the letters of the pen are broken apart and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird's action involving a split reed pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges REED PEN; 'with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird tidies its feathers with its beak; past tense, as 'did' requires.

clue.text: He makes his appeal in a front page article

indicators.note: the front of the word is its opening letter

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's leading article

explanation.surface: Someone appealing for support in a newspaper's front-page piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' takes P from page; LEADER is a leading article, an editorial. 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate who argues a case in court is one who pleads before the judge.

clue.text: Hardy fellow is to speculate about the returned party note

indicators.note: the word for speculating goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to wonder is to speculate

indicators.note: the word for a party is turned back to front

parts.note: a do is a party
la is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tough man is to ponder what went on at the party after it came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' is not tough but Thomas Hardy, author of The Woodlanders. 'returned' reverses the party only; 'about' puts that and the note inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel The Woodlanders features forest dwellers, so a character of his.

clue.text: Duck as it goes into port

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

indicators.note: the letters go into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duck enters the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' rearranges AS IT to STIA after O, the cricket duck (no runs). This was the ancient harbour of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Rome's harbour town at the Tiber's mouth was its seaport.

clue.text: War spoils

definitions.meaning: the Roman god of war, standing for war itself

explanation.surface: Conflict ruins things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of war; also a verb meaning damages or blemishes.

clue.text: Afflictions come a second after love returns

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the word for love is turned round

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
s is the abbreviation for a second

explanation.surface: Troubles arrive a moment after a lover comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns EROS round; 'come' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful inflamed spots, or figuratively grievances, are troubles that afflict someone.

clue.text: Election candidate needs a key, to this squalid housing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Election candidate needs a key, to this squalid housing', gives no workable route to SLUM: no reading of 'Election candidate' or 'a key' yields the letters; likely garbled in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Election candidate needs a key, to this squalid housing

clue.text: Do a turn awkwardly in a kind of building

indicators.note: done awkwardly suggests the letters clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Perform a clumsy pirouette in some structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges DO A TURN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A round domed hall or structure is one type of edifice.

clue.text: Informer who gives back a story in a bar

indicators.note: the whole assembly is given back, read in reverse
the story goes inside the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A grass who hands back a tale in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives back' reverses the whole assembly once 'in' has put the story inside. 'bar' looks like a pub; it is a rod. 'who' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser or denouncer, especially one who reports people to the authorities.

clue.text: Royal accommodation is kept separate in announcements

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other
one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: statements are announcements
apart means separate

explanation.surface: Palace quarters are kept apart in official notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal accommodation' means the grand ceremonial rooms of a palace; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The grand formal rooms of a palace used for ceremonial occasions.
